market_context: United States/general English; home cooking of dried chickpeas
title: Do chickpeas need to be soaked before cooking?

seo.title: Do chickpeas need soaking before cooking?
seo.meta_description: Chickpeas can be cooked without soaking, but several hours in water can greatly shorten cooking and improve hydration, texture and consistency.
seo.search_intent: Learn whether dried chickpeas require soaking, how long to soak them and what soaking changes in cooking and digestibility.

excerpt: Soaking is not an absolute requirement for chickpeas, but it is particularly useful. Several hours in water hydrate the seed before cooking, shorten stove time and can reduce some soluble phytate and raffinose-family oligosaccharides.
content_html:
Chickpeas are larger and denser than lentils, so soaking makes a much bigger practical difference. You can cook chickpeas from dry, but presoaking usually gives faster and more even softening.

What soaking does

Water moves into the seed before heat is applied. FAO describes soaking periods of roughly 4–8 hours for many pulses, while an overnight soak of about 8–12 hours is a convenient household routine for chickpeas.

A prehydrated chickpea needs less stove time for its center to soften than a completely dry one.

Can you skip the soak?

Yes. Dried chickpeas will eventually cook with enough water and time. The tradeoff is a longer cooking process and sometimes less even softening, especially with large or older chickpeas.

A pressure cooker narrows the gap because the higher cooking temperature speeds softening substantially.

Soaking also changes soluble compounds

Some raffinose-family oligosaccharides and other soluble compounds move into the soaking water. Studies of chickpeas show that soaking plus cooking can reduce these fermentable carbohydrates and some phytate.

That may improve digestive comfort for some people, but it does not remove all fermentable fiber from chickpeas.

Should you discard the soaking water?

If your goal is to remove part of what has leached into the water, drain and rinse the chickpeas and cook them in fresh water. Reusing the soak retains more of those soluble compounds.

What about baking soda?

Baking soda raises pH and speeds cell-wall softening, so it can be useful for very tender chickpeas or hummus. Too much can make skins break down quickly and can change flavor. Plain water is sufficient for routine soaking.

Older chickpeas can stay hard

Long storage under warm or humid conditions can contribute to the hard-to-cook phenomenon. Presoaking helps hydration, but very old chickpeas may still take far longer to soften than a fresh batch.

A simple routine

Cover chickpeas with plenty of water before bed, drain them the next day and cook in fresh water. If you make a large batch, cooked chickpeas freeze well in meal-size portions.

Bottom line

Chickpeas do not require soaking for safety, but soaking is usually worth it for time and texture. Several hours of prehydration make cooking faster and more predictable.

faq.question: How long should chickpeas soak?
faq.answer: An overnight 8–12 hour soak is convenient; FAO describes roughly 4–8 hours as a common soaking range for many pulses.

faq.question: Can I cook chickpeas without soaking?
faq.answer: Yes, but they generally take much longer to soften, especially if the chickpeas are large or old.

faq.question: Should I discard chickpea soaking water?
faq.answer: If you want to remove some oligosaccharides and other soluble compounds that leached out, drain it and cook with fresh water.
